message.content:
Based on my research, I can explain how BIOS is installed on a motherboard. There are two different aspects to this: (1) how BIOS comes pre-installed on a new motherboard from the factory, and (2) how users can update/flash BIOS firmware on an existing motherboard.

## How BIOS Comes Pre-Installed on a Motherboard

**Factory Installation:**
- The BIOS (Basic Input/Output System) is stored on a **non-volatile memory chip** (typically a flash memory chip like EEPROM or NOR flash) that is **soldered directly onto the motherboard** during manufacturing
- Motherboard manufacturers program the BIOS firmware onto this chip at the factory before the board is shipped
- The chip retains its data even when power is removed, thanks to the nature of flash memory technology
- Some motherboards also have a **CMOS battery** (a small coin-cell battery) that powers a separate memory area where user-configured BIOS settings are stored

**The BIOS Chip's Role:**
- The BIOS chip contains the firmware that performs the **Power-On Self-Test (POST)** when you turn on the computer
- It initializes all hardware components (CPU, memory, storage devices, etc.)
- It locates and loads the operating system's bootloader
- It provides the setup utility that allows users to configure system settings

## How to Update/Flash BIOS on an Existing Motherboard

If you need to install a newer version of BIOS (called "flashing"), there are several methods:

### Method 1: BIOS Built-in Update Utility (Recommended)
Most modern motherboards include a built-in BIOS update tool:

| Manufacturer | Tool Name | How to Access |
|-------------|-----------|---------------|
| ASUS | EZ Flash | Enter BIOS setup (press DEL/F2 during boot) → Tools section |
| Gigabyte | Q-Flash | Press F9 during POST or access from BIOS menu |
| MSI | M-Flash | Enter BIOS setup → find M-Flash option |
| ASRock | Instant Flash | Enter BIOS → Tool section |

**General Steps:**
1. Download the correct BIOS file from the manufacturer's website for your exact motherboard model
2. Extract the file and copy it to a **FAT32-formatted USB drive**
3. Enter the BIOS setup by pressing the appropriate key during boot (usually DEL, F2, or F12)
4. Launch the BIOS update utility
5. Select the BIOS file from your USB drive
6. Confirm and wait for the update to complete — **do not power off during this process**
7. The system will reboot automatically when finished

### Method 2: Windows-Based Utilities
- ASUS: AI Suite 3 with EZ Update
- Gigabyte: @BIOS utility
- MSI: Live Update

These allow updating from within Windows, but are generally considered riskier because Windows could crash during the process and potentially "brick" the motherboard.

### Method 3: BIOS Flashback Button (For Recovery)
Many modern motherboards have a **BIOS Flashback** button on the rear I/O panel. This allows you to update the BIOS even if the system won't boot:
1. Download and rename the BIOS file according to manufacturer instructions
2. Copy to FAT32 USB drive
3. Insert USB into the designated Flashback port
4. Press the Flashback button
5. Wait for the LED to stop flashing

## Important Warnings

- **Never interrupt a BIOS flash** — power loss during updating can render the motherboard unbootable
- Always use the **exact BIOS file for your specific motherboard model and revision**
- Only update BIOS if necessary (fixing bugs, adding CPU compatibility, etc.)
- Some manufacturers recommend loading **optimized defaults** after a BIOS update

6. https://psbios.me/asus-motherboard-bios-update/
7. https://betasimracing.com/how-to-enter-motherboard-bios/
8. https://www.madpenguin.org/how-to-enter-bios-gigabyte-motherboard/
